title: Student loans in bankruptcy - basics
facts: Student loans covered by Bankruptcy Code section 523(a)(8) are generally not discharged in bankruptcy unless the debtor obtains a court determination that repayment would impose undue hardship.
A debtor seeking an undue-hardship discharge generally must bring an adversary proceeding in the bankruptcy case.

Federal guidance provides a standardized Justice Department and Education Department process for evaluating undue-hardship cases involving federal student loans, but the bankruptcy court makes the legal determination.
Bankruptcy therefore should not be described as automatically erasing federal student loan debt.
